rules.rule_name: Reporting Date Range Parameter Loading
rules.rule_description: The program reads the Date Parameter file at startup to establish the reporting period boundaries (start date and end date) that will be used to filter transactions throughout the report generation process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2: Date Range Parameter Loading
Read reporting start date and end date

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Date Parameter file is available and contains a valid reporting period record with a start date and an end date
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads the Date Parameter file at the beginning of execution
acceptance_criteria.Then: The reporting start date (WS-START-DATE) and reporting end date (WS-END-DATE) are loaded into working storage, and the program displays the message 'Reporting from [Start Date] to [End Date]' confirming the active reporting period

rules.rule_name: Transaction Date Range Filtering
rules.rule_description: Each transaction read from the transaction file is evaluated against the reporting date range. Only transactions whose processing date falls within the defined start and end dates (inclusive) are included in the report; all others are skipped.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4: Transaction Date
Range Filtering
Is transaction date within
reporting date range?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the Transaction file and the reporting start date and end date have been loaded from the Date Parameter file
acceptance_criteria.When: The first 10 characters of the transaction processing timestamp (TRAN-PROC-TS) are compared against the reporting start date (WS-START-DATE) and end date (WS-END-DATE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the transaction processing date is greater than or equal to the start date AND less than or equal to the end date, the transaction is included in the report; otherwise the transaction is skipped and the next transaction is read

rules.rule_name: Card Number Change Detection
rules.rule_description: As transactions are processed sequentially, the program detects when the card number on the current transaction differs from the card number of the previously processed transaction, signaling a transition to a new card/account group.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5: Card Number
Change Detection
Is current card number
different from previous?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has passed the date range filter and is within the reporting period, and a current card number (WS-CURR-CARD-NUM) is being tracked
acceptance_criteria.When: The card number on the current transaction (TRAN-CARD-NUM) is compared to the previously tracked card number (WS-CURR-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card numbers are different, a card number change is detected and the program proceeds to write account totals for the previous card group (if applicable) and then performs a cross-reference lookup for the new card number; if the card numbers are the same, the program proceeds directly to transaction type lookup without writing account totals

rules.rule_name: Account Total Writing on Card Group Change
rules.rule_description: When a new card number group begins and it is not the very first transaction being processed, the accumulated total for the completed card/account group is written to the report and then reset to zero to begin accumulation for the new account group.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6: Account Total Writing
Write accumulated total for
previous account and reset to zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card number change has been detected and the first-time processing flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is set to 'N', indicating at least one prior card group has been processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program writes the account totals for the completed card group
acceptance_criteria.Then: The accumulated account total (WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL) is moved to the report account total field (REPT-ACCOUNT-TOTAL), the account total line is written to the Report file, the account total accumulator (WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL) is reset to zero, the line counter is incremented by 1, and a column header separator line (TRANSACTION-HEADER-2) is written to the Report file

rules.rule_name: Card-to-Account Cross-Reference Lookup
rules.rule_description: When a new card number is encountered, the program looks up the card number in the Card Cross-Reference file to retrieve the associated Account ID, which will be printed on every transaction detail line within that card group.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7: Card-to-Account
Cross-Reference Lookup
Lookup card number to retrieve
associated account ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new card number (TRAN-CARD-NUM) has been identified, the card number has been set as the current card number (WS-CURR-CARD-NUM), and the card number has been moved to the cross-reference lookup key (FD-XREF-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program performs a direct lookup of the Card Cross-Reference file (XREF-FILE) using the card number as the key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cross-reference record (CARD-XREF-RECORD) is retrieved and the associated Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID) is available for use on transaction detail lines for all transactions belonging to this card number

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Description Lookup
rules.rule_description: For every qualifying transaction, the transaction type code is used to look up the corresponding human-readable transaction type description from the Transaction Type reference file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8: Transaction Type
Description Lookup
Lookup transaction type code
to get description

acceptance_criteria.Given: A qualifying transaction record is being processed and the transaction type code (TRAN-TYPE-CD from TRAN-RECORD) has been moved to the Transaction Type file lookup key (FD-TRAN-TYPE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program performs a direct lookup of the Transaction Type file (TRANTYPE-FILE) using the transaction type code as the key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction type record (TRAN-TYPE-RECORD) is retrieved and the transaction type description (TRAN-TYPE-DESC) is available to be printed on the transaction detail line

rules.rule_name: Transaction Category Description Lookup
rules.rule_description: For every qualifying transaction, the combination of transaction type code and transaction category code is used to look up the corresponding category description from the Transaction Category reference file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9: Transaction Category
Description Lookup
Lookup type and category code
to get category description

acceptance_criteria.Given: A qualifying transaction record is being processed, the transaction type code (TRAN-TYPE-CD from TRAN-RECORD) has been moved to FD-TRAN-TYPE-CD within FD-TRAN-CAT-KEY, and the transaction category code (TRAN-CAT-CD from TRAN-RECORD) has been moved to FD-TRAN-CAT-CD within FD-TRAN-CAT-KEY
acceptance_criteria.When: The program performs a direct lookup of the Transaction Category file (TRANCATG-FILE) using the composite key of transaction type code plus transaction category code (FD-TRAN-CAT-KEY)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction category record (TRAN-CAT-RECORD) is retrieved and the transaction category description (TRAN-CAT-TYPE-DESC) is available to be printed on the transaction detail line

rules.rule_name: Report Header Writing on First Transaction
rules.rule_description: When the very first qualifying transaction is about to be written to the report, the program initializes the report by writing the report headers including the reporting date range, before writing any transaction detail lines.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Report Header Writing
First transaction or
new page needed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A qualifying transaction is ready to be written to the report and the first-time flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is set to 'Y', indicating no transactions have been written yet
acceptance_criteria.When: The program checks the first-time flag before writing the transaction detail
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first-time flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is set to 'N', the reporting start date (WS-START-DATE) is moved to the report start date field (REPT-START-DATE), the reporting end date (WS-END-DATE) is moved to the report end date field (REPT-END-DATE), and the report headers are written to the Report file

rules.rule_name: Report Header Content and Structure
rules.rule_description: The report header section written at the start of the report and at the top of each new page consists of four lines: the report name header, a blank separator line, and two column header lines.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Write Report Headers
Report name, blank line,
column headers with date range

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has determined that report headers need to be written (either first transaction or new page)
acceptance_criteria.When: The report header writing procedure is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: Four lines are written sequentially to the Report file: (1) the Report Name Header line (REPORT-NAME-HEADER), (2) a blank line (WS-BLANK-LINE), (3) the first column header line (TRANSACTION-HEADER-1), and (4) the second column header line (TRANSACTION-HEADER-2); the line counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1 for each line written, totaling 4 increments

rules.rule_name: Page Break Detection and Page Total Writing
rules.rule_description: After headers are confirmed, the program checks whether the current page is full by evaluating if the line counter has reached the configured page size. If the page is full, page totals are written, the page total is added to the grand total, the page total is reset, and new column headers are written for the next page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: Page Break Check
Line counter reached
page size of 20?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A qualifying transaction is being processed and the line counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) and page size (WS-PAGE-SIZE) are available
acceptance_criteria.When: The remainder of dividing the line counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) by the page size (WS-PAGE-SIZE) equals zero (FUNCTION MOD(WS-LINE-COUNTER, WS-PAGE-SIZE) = 0)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page total writing procedure is invoked: the current page total (WS-PAGE-TOTAL) is moved to the report page total field (REPT-PAGE-TOTAL), the page total line (REPORT-PAGE-TOTALS) is written to the Report file, the page total (WS-PAGE-TOTAL) is added to the grand total (WS-GRAND-TOTAL), the page total accumulator (WS-PAGE-TOTAL) is reset to zero, the line counter is incremented by 1, a column header separator line (TRANSACTION-HEADER-2) is written to the Report file, the line counter is incremented by 1 again, and then new report headers are written

rules.rule_name: Transaction Amount Accumulation into Page and Account Totals
rules.rule_description: For every qualifying transaction that passes all checks, the transaction amount is simultaneously added to both the running page total and the running account total accumulators.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12: Transaction Amount Accumulation
Add transaction amount to
page total and account total

acceptance_criteria.Given: A qualifying transaction record has passed date range filtering, card number processing, reference lookups, header checks, and page break checks
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction amount (TRAN-AMT) is accumulated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction amount (TRAN-AMT) is added to the page total accumulator (WS-PAGE-TOTAL) AND simultaneously added to the account total accumulator (WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL) in a single ADD operation

rules.rule_name: Transaction Detail Line Content and Writing
rules.rule_description: For each qualifying transaction, a formatted detail line is written to the report containing all relevant transaction information including the account ID resolved from the card cross-reference lookup.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13: Transaction Detail Line Writing
Write transaction ID, account ID,
type, category, source, amount

acceptance_criteria.Given: A qualifying transaction has been accumulated into page and account totals, and all reference lookups (account ID, type description, category description) have been completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction detail line is composed and written to the Report file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The TRANSACTION-DETAIL-REPORT record is initialized, and the following fields are populated and written as a single detail line to the Report file: Transaction ID (TRAN-ID → TRAN-REPORT-TRANS-ID), Account ID from cross-reference (XREF-ACCT-ID → TRAN-REPORT-ACCOUNT-ID), Transaction Type Code (TRAN-TYPE-CD → TRAN-REPORT-TYPE-CD), Transaction Type Description (TRAN-TYPE-DESC → TRAN-REPORT-TYPE-DESC), Transaction Category Code (TRAN-CAT-CD → TRAN-REPORT-CAT-CD), Transaction Category Description (TRAN-CAT-TYPE-DESC → TRAN-REPORT-CAT-DESC), Transaction Source (TRAN-SOURCE → TRAN-REPORT-SOURCE), Transaction Amount (TRAN-AMT → TRAN-REPORT-AMT); the line counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1 after writing

rules.rule_name: End-of-File Final Page Total Writing
rules.rule_description: When the end of the transaction file is reached, the program writes the final page total for the last page of the report and adds it to the grand total before writing the grand total line.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14: End-of-File Page Total Writing
Write final page total and
add to grand total

acceptance_criteria.Given: The end of the Transaction file has been reached (END-OF-FILE = 'Y') after reading a transaction record
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is detected within the processing loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction amount (TRAN-AMT) is added to the page total (WS-PAGE-TOTAL) and account total (WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL), then the final page total writing procedure is invoked: the current page total (WS-PAGE-TOTAL) is moved to REPT-PAGE-TOTAL, the page total line (REPORT-PAGE-TOTALS) is written to the Report file, the page total (WS-PAGE-TOTAL) is added to the grand total (WS-GRAND-TOTAL), the page total accumulator is reset to zero, the line counter is incremented, and a column header separator line (TRANSACTION-HEADER-2) is written

rules.rule_name: Grand Total Writing at End of Report
rules.rule_description: After all page totals have been written and accumulated, the overall grand total representing the sum of all transaction amounts across the entire reporting period is written as the final line of the report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15: Grand Total Writing
Write accumulated grand total
for all transactions

acceptance_criteria.Given: All transactions have been processed, the final page total has been written and added to the grand total accumulator (WS-GRAND-TOTAL)
acceptance_criteria.When: The grand total writing procedure is executed after the final page total writing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The accumulated grand total (WS-GRAND-TOTAL) is moved to the report grand total field (REPT-GRAND-TOTAL), and the grand total line (REPORT-GRAND-TOTALS) is written to the Report file as the final entry in the report

rules.rule_name: Report Processing Sequence and Program Lifecycle
rules.rule_description: The program follows a strict sequential lifecycle: all required input and output files must be opened before any processing begins, and all files must be closed after all processing and report writing is complete.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1: Program Initialization
Open all required input and output files

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program CBTRN03C is invoked for execution
acceptance_criteria.When: The program starts and completes its execution lifecycle
acceptance_criteria.Then: At startup, all six files are opened in the following order: Transaction file (input), Report file (output), Card Cross-Reference file (input), Transaction Type file (input), Transaction Category file (input), and Date Parameter file (input); at completion, all six files are closed in the following order: Transaction file, Report file, Card Cross-Reference file, Transaction Type file, Transaction Category file, and Date Parameter file; the program displays 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBTRN03C' at the beginning and 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBTRN03C' at the end

acceptance_criteria.When: The Date Parameter file read is successful and a record is found (file status is '00')
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Reporting Start Date (WS-START-DATE) and Reporting End Date (WS-END-DATE) are loaded into working memory from the date parameter record, and processing continues to display the date range

rules.rule_name: Display Confirmed Reporting Date Range
rules.rule_description: After successfully loading the date parameters, the program confirms the active reporting period by displaying the start date and end date that will be used to filter transactions for the report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Reporting Date Range: Start Date to End Date

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Reporting Start Date and Reporting End Date have been successfully loaded from the Date Parameter file
acceptance_criteria.When: The date parameter record is found and loaded without errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'Reporting from [WS-START-DATE] to [WS-END-DATE]' to confirm the active reporting date range before transaction processing begins

rules.rule_name: Halt Processing When No Date Parameter Record Exists
rules.rule_description: If the Date Parameter file contains no records (end-of-file condition), the program cannot determine the reporting date range and must stop all transaction processing immediately.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was date parameter record found?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to read the Date Parameter file
acceptance_criteria.When: The Date Parameter file read returns an end-of-file condition (file status is '10'), meaning no date parameter record exists
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End-of-File indicator (END-OF-FILE) is set to 'Y', which prevents any transaction processing from occurring and causes the program to proceed directly to closing all files and ending execution

rules.rule_name: Halt Processing on Date Parameter File Read Failure
rules.rule_description: If the Date Parameter file cannot be read due to an unexpected error, the program cannot reliably determine the reporting date range and must immediately stop execution to prevent generating an incorrect or incomplete report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was date parameter record found?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to read the Date Parameter file
acceptance_criteria.When: The Date Parameter file read returns an unexpected error condition (file status is neither '00' for success nor '10' for end-of-file)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program displays the error message 'ERROR READING DATEPARM FILE', records the file status for diagnostic display, and immediately terminates program execution abnormally — no transaction processing or report generation occurs

rules.rule_name: Sequential Reading of Transaction Records from Transaction File
rules.rule_description: The program reads transaction records one at a time, sequentially from the Transaction File into the Transaction Record buffer (TRAN-RECORD) for downstream processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Next Transaction Record from Transaction File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction File has been successfully opened for input and the end-of-file flag is set to 'N' (not yet reached end of file)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program requests the next transaction record from the Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next available transaction record is read sequentially from the Transaction File and loaded into the Transaction Record (TRAN-RECORD) for processing

rules.rule_name: Transaction Record Successfully Read and Available for Processing
rules.rule_description: When a transaction record is read without any issues, the record is confirmed as available and the program proceeds with transaction processing logic.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Record Read Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed against the Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction File read operation completes successfully (file status indicates a normal successful read)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction record is confirmed as available and ready for processing; the program continues to the next processing step without interruption

rules.rule_name: End-of-File Detected on Transaction File - Mark Processing Complete
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction File has no more records to read, the program detects the end-of-file condition and marks the end-of-file flag to signal that all transactions have been processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End of File Reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed against the Transaction File and the read was not successful
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction File read operation returns an end-of-file condition (no more transaction records exist in the file)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag (END-OF-FILE) is set to 'Y', signaling that all transactions have been read and no further transaction records are available for processing; the processing loop will terminate

rules.rule_name: No More Transactions Available - End Processing Loop
rules.rule_description: Once the end-of-file flag is set to 'Y', the main transaction processing loop recognizes that all transactions have been consumed and stops requesting further records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark End-of-File Flag as Yes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The End-of-File flag (END-OF-FILE) has been set to 'Y' after detecting end-of-file on the Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.When: The main processing loop evaluates the End-of-File flag at the start of each iteration
acceptance_criteria.Then: The main processing loop terminates because the condition END-OF-FILE = 'Y' is satisfied; no further transaction records are read or processed

rules.rule_name: Transaction Processing Date Extraction from Timestamp
rules.rule_description: The transaction processing date is derived from the first 10 characters of the transaction processing timestamp field. This date value is used as the basis for all date range comparisons during report filtering.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Transaction Processing Date from Transaction Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the Transaction file, and the transaction record contains a processing timestamp field (TRAN-PROC-TS)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to evaluate whether the transaction falls within the reporting date range
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system extracts the first 10 characters of the transaction processing timestamp (TRAN-PROC-TS positions 1 through 10) to represent the transaction processing date, and this extracted date value is used for all subsequent date range comparisons

rules.rule_name: Transaction Processing Date Must Be On or After Reporting Start Date
rules.rule_description: Each transaction's processing date is compared against the reporting period start date. Transactions processed before the reporting start date are excluded from the report and the program moves on to read the next transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Transaction Date greater than or equal to Reporting Start Date?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the Transaction file, the transaction processing date has been extracted from the first 10 characters of the processing timestamp (TRAN-PROC-TS), and the reporting start date (WS-START-DATE) has been loaded from the Date Parameters file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the transaction processing date against the reporting start date
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the transaction processing date is less than the reporting start date, the transaction is skipped and excluded from the report, and the program proceeds to read the next transaction; if the transaction processing date is greater than or equal to the reporting start date, the transaction passes the lower bound check and proceeds to the end date comparison

rules.rule_name: Transaction Processing Date Must Be On or Before Reporting End Date
rules.rule_description: Each transaction's processing date is compared against the reporting period end date. Transactions processed after the reporting end date are excluded from the report and the program moves on to read the next transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Transaction Date less than or equal to Reporting End Date?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the Transaction file, the transaction processing date has been extracted from the first 10 characters of the processing timestamp (TRAN-PROC-TS), the transaction has already passed the start date check, and the reporting end date (WS-END-DATE) has been loaded from the Date Parameters file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the transaction processing date against the reporting end date
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the transaction processing date is greater than the reporting end date, the transaction is skipped and excluded from the report, and the program proceeds to read the next transaction; if the transaction processing date is less than or equal to the reporting end date, the transaction passes the upper bound check and qualifies for inclusion in the report

rules.rule_name: Transaction Date Range Qualification - Both Bounds Must Be Satisfied
rules.rule_description: A transaction is included in the report only when its processing date satisfies both the lower bound (on or after start date) and the upper bound (on or before end date) conditions simultaneously. Both conditions must be true for the transaction to qualify for reporting.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transaction Qualifies for Reporting

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the Transaction file, the transaction processing date has been extracted from the first 10 characters of the processing timestamp (TRAN-PROC-TS), and both the reporting start date (WS-START-DATE) and reporting end date (WS-END-DATE) have been loaded from the Date Parameters file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the combined date range condition: transaction processing date is greater than or equal to WS-START-DATE AND transaction processing date is less than or equal to WS-END-DATE
acceptance_criteria.Then: If both conditions are true simultaneously, the transaction qualifies for reporting and processing continues to the card number processing step; if either condition is false (date is before start date OR date is after end date), the transaction is skipped entirely and the program returns to read the next transaction record from the Transaction file

rules.rule_name: Skip Out-of-Range Transaction and Return to Next Transaction Read
rules.rule_description: When a transaction's processing date falls outside the specified reporting date range (either before the start date or after the end date), the transaction is completely bypassed with no processing, no totals accumulation, and no report output generated for that transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Skip Transaction Outside Date Range

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the Transaction file, and the transaction processing date extracted from the first 10 characters of TRAN-PROC-TS has been evaluated against the reporting date range defined by WS-START-DATE and WS-END-DATE
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction processing date is either strictly less than the reporting start date (WS-START-DATE) or strictly greater than the reporting end date (WS-END-DATE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction is skipped with no further processing performed — no cross-reference lookup, no transaction type lookup, no transaction category lookup, no detail line written to the report, and no amounts added to page total or account total; the program immediately proceeds to read the next transaction record from the Transaction file

key_functionalities.title: Card Number Change Detection
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Qualifying Transaction\nAvailable for Processing])
    B{Is Current Card Number\ndifferent from\nPreviously Processed\nCard Number?}
    C{Is this the\nFirst Transaction\nBeing Processed?}
    D[Write Accumulated Total\nfor Previous Account Group\nand Reset Account Total to Zero]
    E[Update Stored Card Number\nto Current Transaction\nCard Number]
    F[Lookup Account ID\nfor New Card Number\nvia Cross-Reference]
    G[Continue Processing\nSame Account Group]
    H([Proceed to Transaction\nType Lookup])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - New Card Number Detected\nNew Account Group Starting| C
    B -->|No - Same Card Number\nSame Account Group| G
    C -->|No - Previous Account\nGroup Exists| D
    D --> E
    C -->|Yes - No Previous\nAccount Group| E
    E --> F
    F --> H
    G --> H

rules.rule_name: Detect New Card Number to Identify New Account Group
rules.rule_description: When processing each qualifying transaction, the program compares the card number on the current transaction against the card number of the previously processed transaction to determine whether a new account group has started.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Current Card Number different from Previously Processed Card Number?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A qualifying transaction has passed the date range filter and is available for processing, and a previously processed card number is stored in memory (WS-CURR-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The card number on the current transaction (TRAN-CARD-NUM) is compared against the stored previously processed card number (WS-CURR-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card numbers are different, a new account group is detected and the program initiates account group transition processing; if the card numbers are the same, the transaction belongs to the current account group and processing continues without any account group transition

rules.rule_name: Guard Against Writing Account Totals Before First Transaction is Processed
rules.rule_description: When a new card number is detected, the program must determine whether a previous account group actually exists before attempting to write account totals. This prevents writing empty or invalid account totals at the very start of report generation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this the First Transaction Being Processed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new card number has been detected on the current transaction, indicating a potential account group transition
acceptance_criteria.When: The program checks the first-time processing indicator (WS-FIRST-TIME) to determine if any previous account group has been processed
acceptance_criteria.Then: If WS-FIRST-TIME is 'N' (not the first transaction), a previous account group exists and account totals must be written for it before starting the new group; if WS-FIRST-TIME is 'Y' (first transaction), no previous account group exists and writing account totals is skipped, proceeding directly to update the stored card number

rules.rule_name: Write Accumulated Account Total and Reset for New Account Group
rules.rule_description: When a previous account group exists and a new card number is detected, the accumulated transaction total for the completed account group is written to the report and the account total accumulator is reset to zero in preparation for the new account group.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Accumulated Total for Previous Account Group and Reset Account Total to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new card number has been detected and the first-time indicator confirms a previous account group was processed (WS-FIRST-TIME = 'N'), with a non-zero accumulated account total (WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL) representing the sum of all transaction amounts for the previous card group
acceptance_criteria.When: The account totals writing process is triggered for the completed account group
acceptance_criteria.Then: The accumulated account total (WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL) is moved to the report account total field (REPT-ACCOUNT-TOTAL), the account totals line is written to the report file, the account total accumulator (WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL) is reset to zero, the line counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1, a column separator header line (TRANSACTION-HEADER-2) is written to the report, and the line counter is incremented by 1 again

rules.rule_name: Update Stored Card Number to Current Transaction Card Number
rules.rule_description: After handling the previous account group totals (or at the start of the first group), the program updates its stored current card number to the card number of the new transaction, establishing the new account group context for subsequent transactions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update Stored Card Number to Current Transaction Card Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new card number has been detected on the current transaction, and any required account totals for the previous group have already been written (or skipped for the first transaction)
acceptance_criteria.When: The stored current card number is updated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card number from the current transaction (TRAN-CARD-NUM) is copied into the stored current card number field (WS-CURR-CARD-NUM), establishing the new account group identity for all subsequent transactions until the next card number change is detected

rules.rule_name: Set Card Number as Cross-Reference Lookup Key for Account ID Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When a new card number is established, the card number must be used as the key to look up the associated Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference file, so that the Account ID can be printed on all transaction detail lines within this account group.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Lookup Account ID for New Card Number via Cross-Reference

acceptance_criteria.Given: The stored current card number (WS-CURR-CARD-NUM) has been updated to the new transaction's card number (TRAN-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The cross-reference lookup is initiated for the new card number
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction card number (TRAN-CARD-NUM) is moved into the cross-reference file lookup key field (FD-XREF-CARD-NUM), and the cross-reference lookup process is invoked to retrieve the Account ID associated with that card number

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Account ID from Card Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: The Card Cross-Reference file is read using the card number as the key to retrieve the Account ID record. If the card number does not exist in the cross-reference file, the transaction is considered invalid and processing cannot continue.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Lookup Account ID for New Card Number via Cross-Reference

acceptance_criteria.Given: The cross-reference file lookup key (FD-XREF-CARD-NUM) has been set to the new card number, and the Card Cross-Reference file (XREF-FILE) is open and available
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Cross-Reference file is read using the card number as the key
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card number is found, the full cross-reference record (CARD-XREF-RECORD) including the Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID) is retrieved and made available for use on transaction detail lines; if the card number is NOT found in the cross-reference file, the transaction is flagged as having an invalid card number, an 'INVALID CARD NUMBER' message is displayed along with the card number, and the program terminates abnormally as the data integrity cannot be guaranteed

rules.rule_name: Continue Processing Same Account Group Without Account Total Write
rules.rule_description: When the card number on the current transaction matches the previously processed card number, the transaction belongs to the same account group and no account group transition actions are required — processing proceeds directly to transaction type lookup.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Continue Processing Same Account Group

acceptance_criteria.Given: A qualifying transaction has passed the date range filter and is available for processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The card number on the current transaction (TRAN-CARD-NUM) is equal to the stored previously processed card number (WS-CURR-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.Then: No account group transition actions are performed — no account totals are written, no card number update occurs, and no cross-reference lookup is triggered; the program proceeds directly to the transaction type lookup step for the current transaction

key_functionalities.title: Account Total Writing
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:

    A([New Transaction Read

rules.rule_name: Detect Card Number Change to Trigger Account Group Boundary
rules.rule_description: When processing transactions sequentially, the program must detect when a transaction belongs to a different card than the previous transaction, signaling the end of one account group and the beginning of another.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Current Card Number Different from Previous Card Number?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction has been read from the transaction file and its processing date has been validated to fall within the reporting date range, and a previous card number is being tracked in the current card number field
acceptance_criteria.When: The card number on the current transaction is compared to the previously tracked card number, and the two values are NOT equal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program identifies this as a card number change event and triggers the account group boundary processing, which includes writing account totals for the previous card group and updating the tracked card number to the new card number

rules.rule_name: Suppress Account Total Writing for the First Transaction of the Report
rules.rule_description: When a card number change is detected, the program must determine whether a previous account group actually exists before attempting to write account totals. On the very first transaction of the report, there is no prior account group, so writing account totals must be suppressed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this the First Transaction of the Report?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card number change has been detected on the current transaction, and the first-time processing indicator is being evaluated
acceptance_criteria.When: The first-time processing indicator is set to 'Y', meaning this is the very first card number encountered in the current report run
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program skips writing account totals entirely (no account total line is written to the report) and proceeds directly to updating the current card number to the new card number

rules.rule_name: Write Accumulated Account Total for Previous Card Group
rules.rule_description: When a card number change is detected and a previous account group exists, the accumulated transaction total for that account group must be retrieved and written to the report before processing begins for the new card group.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Accumulated Account Total for Previous Card/Account

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card number change has been detected, the first-time indicator is 'N' confirming a previous account group exists, and the account total field holds the sum of all transaction amounts processed for the previous card number
acceptance_criteria.When: The account total writing process is triggered for the previous card group
acceptance_criteria.Then: The accumulated account total amount is moved into the report account total field, the formatted account total line is written to the report output file

rules.rule_name: Reset Account Total to Zero After Writing
rules.rule_description: After the account total for the previous card group has been written to the report, the account total accumulator must be reset to zero so that it can begin accumulating transaction amounts for the new card group without carrying over amounts from the previous group.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Account Total to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account total line for the previous card group has been successfully written to the report
acceptance_criteria.When: The account total reset step is executed as part of the account total writing process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The account total accumulator is set to zero, ensuring that transaction amounts for the upcoming new card group are accumulated independently from the previous card group

rules.rule_name: Write Separator Line After Account Total
rules.rule_description: After the account total line is written and the accumulator is reset, a separator/column header line must be written to the report to visually separate the completed account group from the next account group's transactions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Separator Line to Report

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account total line has been written to the report and the account total accumulator has been reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The separator line writing step is executed as part of the account total writing process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The column header line 2 (used as a separator) is written to the report output file and the line counter is incremented by one to reflect the additional line written

rules.rule_name: Update Tracked Card Number to New Card Number
rules.rule_description: After completing all account total writing for the previous card group (or immediately on the first transaction), the program must update its tracked current card number to the new card number so that subsequent transactions can be correctly grouped under the new card.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update Current Card Number to New Card Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: Either the account totals for the previous card group have been written and reset, or this is the first transaction of the report, and the new card number from the current transaction is available
acceptance_criteria.When: The card number update step is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current card number tracker is updated to hold the new transaction's card number, and the card cross-reference lookup key is also set to the new card number so that the account ID associated with the new card can be retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference file

key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:

    START([Start: Card-to-Account\nCross-Reference Lookup])

rules.rule_name: Set Card Number as Cross-Reference Lookup Key
rules.rule_description: When a transaction belongs to a new card number (different from the previously processed card), the transaction's card number must be established as both the current tracking card number and the key used to search the Card Cross-Reference file for the associated account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Current Card Number to Transaction Card Number and use as Lookup Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the Transaction file, and the transaction's Card Number (TRAN-CARD-NUM) is different from the currently tracked Card Number (WS-CURR-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects a card number change and prepares to look up the account associated with the new card number
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction's Card Number (TRAN-CARD-NUM) must be stored as the new current Card Number (WS-CURR-CARD-NUM) and simultaneously set as the lookup key (FD-XREF-CARD-NUM) for the Card Cross-Reference file search, after which the cross-reference lookup process is invoked

rules.rule_name: Card Number Lookup in Card Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: The system must search the Card Cross-Reference file using the card number as the key to find the associated account. The lookup determines whether the card number is a valid, registered card with a known account mapping.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Lookup Card Number in Card Cross-Reference File XREF-FILE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card number (FD-XREF-CARD-NUM) has been set as the lookup key and the Card Cross-Reference file (XREF-FILE) is open for input
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a direct key-based read of the Card Cross-Reference file (XREF-FILE) using the card number as the search key, retrieving the result into the Card Cross-Reference record (CARD-XREF-RECORD)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card number is found in the file, the associated cross-reference record (CARD-XREF-RECORD) is retrieved successfully and processing continues; if the card number is NOT found (Invalid Key condition), the system identifies the card as unrecognized and halts further processing

rules.rule_name: Invalid Card Number Stops Report Processing
rules.rule_description: Every card number appearing in the transaction file must exist in the Card Cross-Reference file. If a transaction references a card number that cannot be found in the cross-reference, it is considered an unrecognized card and the report generation must be stopped immediately, as the account association cannot be determined.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card Number Not Found in Cross-Reference File Report Invalid Card Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record contains a Card Number (FD-XREF-CARD-NUM) that is being looked up in the Card Cross-Reference file (XREF-FILE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The card number is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file (Invalid Key condition is triggered during the READ of XREF-FILE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'INVALID CARD NUMBER : ' followed by the unrecognized card number (FD-XREF-CARD-NUM), and immediately stop all report processing — no further transactions are processed and no report output is produced for the invalid card or any subsequent records

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Account ID from Cross-Reference Record
rules.rule_description: When a card number is successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file, the associated Account ID must be retrieved from the cross-reference record. This Account ID represents the financial account linked to the card and is the business identifier used throughout the transaction report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Associated Account ID XREF-ACCT-ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference file lookup has completed successfully and the cross-reference record (CARD-XREF-RECORD) has been retrieved for the given card number
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads the Account ID field (XREF-ACCT-ID) from the retrieved cross-reference record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID) is made available for use in transaction reporting, representing the financial account associated with the card number for all transactions in the current card group

rules.rule_name: Account ID Used on Transaction Report Detail Line
rules.rule_description: The Account ID retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference file must be printed on every transaction detail line in the report for the current card group. This ensures each reported transaction is associated with its correct financial account identifier rather than the card number.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Account ID Available for Transaction Reporting

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID) has been retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference file for the current card number, and a qualifying transaction detail line is being prepared for the report
acceptance_criteria.When: The system formats the transaction detail line (TRANSACTION-DETAIL-REPORT) for writing to the report file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID) must be placed in the Account ID field (TRAN-REPORT-ACCOUNT-ID) of the transaction detail report line, so that the report displays the account associated with the card for every transaction in that card group

key_functionalities.title: Transaction Type Description Lookup
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Transaction Type\nDescription Lookup])
    MOVE_TYPE[Extract Transaction Type Code\nfrom Current Transaction Record]
    READ_TRANTYPE[(TRANTYPE-FILE\nTransaction Type\nReference File)]

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the Transaction file and is currently being processed

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Transaction Type Description on Successful Lookup

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Human-Readable Transaction Type Description

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code extracted from the current transaction record is used as the search key against the Transaction Type reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: A matching record is found in the Transaction Type reference file for the given Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Description (TRAN-TYPE-DESC) is successfully retrieved from the reference record and stored for use in the transaction report detail line (TRAN-REPORT-TYPE-DESC)

rules.rule_name: Reject Invalid Transaction Type Code and Stop Processing
rules.rule_description: If a Transaction Type Code from a transaction record does not exist in the Transaction Type reference file, it is considered an invalid code and the report generation must stop immediately, as the transaction cannot be properly described or categorized.

acceptance_criteria.When: No matching record is found in the Transaction Type reference file for the given Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The invalid Transaction Type Code is identified and reported, a message displaying 'INVALID TRANSACTION TYPE' along with the invalid code value is shown, and the program immediately stops all processing — no further transactions are processed and no report output is produced

rules.rule_name: Apply Transaction Type Description to Report Detail Line

acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction detail line is being prepared for writing to the report
acceptance_criteria.Then: The retrieved Transaction Type Description (TRAN-TYPE-DESC) is placed into the Transaction Type Description field (TRAN-REPORT-TYPE-DESC) of the report detail line, ensuring the report displays the full human-readable description alongside the Transaction Type Code

acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Category Description (TRAN-CAT-TYPE-DESC) is available and will be included in the transaction report detail line alongside the Transaction Category Code

rules.rule_name: Detect First Transaction to Trigger Initial Report Header
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the current transaction being processed is the very first transaction in the report run, which triggers the initial report header to be written including the reporting date range.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this the First Transaction? WS-FIRST-TIME = Y

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction report generation process has started and a qualifying transaction within the reporting date range is ready to be written to the report
acceptance_criteria.When: The First Transaction Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is evaluated and its value is 'Y', indicating no transaction has been written to the report yet
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies this as the first transaction, sets the reporting start date and end date into the report header fields, marks the First Transaction Flag as processed (set to 'N'), and proceeds to write the full report header section

rules.rule_name: Set Reporting Date Range in Report Header on First Transaction
rules.rule_description: When the first transaction is being processed, the reporting period start date and end date are captured from the Date Parameters file and placed into the report header fields so they appear on the printed report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Reporting Date Range
Move Start Date and End Date
to Report Header Fields

acceptance_criteria.Given: The First Transaction Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is 'Y', indicating this is the first transaction being written to the report, and the reporting Start Date (WS-START-DATE) and End Date (WS-END-DATE) have been loaded from the Date Parameters file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to write the initial report header for the first time
acceptance_criteria.Then: The reporting Start Date (WS-START-DATE) is moved into the Report Start Date field (REPT-START-DATE) and the reporting End Date (WS-END-DATE) is moved into the Report End Date field (REPT-END-DATE), so the report header displays the correct reporting period

rules.rule_name: Mark First Transaction Flag as Processed After Initial Header
rules.rule_description: After the initial report header has been triggered for the first transaction, the First Transaction Flag is updated to prevent the initial header setup from being repeated for subsequent transactions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark First Transaction
Flag as Processed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The First Transaction Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is currently 'Y' and the reporting date range has been set into the report header fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the first-time header setup before writing the report header lines
acceptance_criteria.Then: The First Transaction Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is set to 'N', ensuring that the date range setup and first-time header logic are not executed again for any subsequent transactions in the same report run

rules.rule_name: Detect Page Size Limit Reached to Trigger New Page Header
rules.rule_description: After the first transaction has been processed, the system checks whether the current page has reached its maximum line capacity. If the page is full, page totals are written and a new page header is started.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Has Page Size
Limit Been Reached?
Line Counter MOD 20 = 0

acceptance_criteria.Given: The First Transaction Flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is 'N', indicating at least one transaction has already been written to the report, and the Line Counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is being tracked
acceptance_criteria.When: The remainder of dividing the current Line Counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) by the Page Size (WS-PAGE-SIZE, which is 20) equals zero, indicating the page line limit has been reached
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system writes the current page totals to the report, resets the page total accumulator to zero, adds the page total to the grand total, and then proceeds to write a new page header section for the next page

rules.rule_name: Write Report Name Header Including Reporting Date Range
rules.rule_description: As the first line of every report header section (both initial and new page headers), the Report Name Header line is written to the report file. On the first page, this header includes the reporting start and end dates.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Write Report Name Header
Including Reporting Start
and End Dates

acceptance_criteria.Given: A report header section needs to be written, either because this is the first transaction (WS-FIRST-TIME was 'Y') or because the page size limit has been reached (Line Counter MOD Page Size = 0), and the Report Name Header record (REPORT-NAME-HEADER) is populated with the report name and reporting date range
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the Write Headers procedure (1120-WRITE-HEADERS)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Report Name Header record (REPORT-NAME-HEADER) is written as the first line of the header section to the report output file, and the Line Counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1

rules.rule_name: Write Blank Line as Second Line of Report Header Section
rules.rule_description: Immediately after the Report Name Header line, a blank line is written to the report to visually separate the report title from the column headers, improving report readability.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Blank Line

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Report Name Header line has been successfully written to the report file and the Line Counter has been incremented
acceptance_criteria.When: The system continues executing the Write Headers procedure (1120-WRITE-HEADERS) after writing the report name header
acceptance_criteria.Then: A blank line (WS-BLANK-LINE) is written as the second line of the header section to the report output file, and the Line Counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1

rules.rule_name: Write Column Header Line 1 as Third Line of Report Header Section
rules.rule_description: After the blank line, the first column header line containing the transaction detail column titles is written to the report, providing labels for each data column in the transaction detail lines.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Write Column Header Line 1
Transaction Details Column Titles

acceptance_criteria.Given: The blank line has been successfully written to the report file and the Line Counter has been incremented
acceptance_criteria.When: The system continues executing the Write Headers procedure (1120-WRITE-HEADERS) after writing the blank line
acceptance_criteria.Then: Column Header Line 1 (TRANSACTION-HEADER-1), containing the transaction detail column titles, is written as the third line of the header section to the report output file, and the Line Counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1

rules.rule_name: Write Column Header Line 2 as Fourth Line of Report Header Section
rules.rule_description: As the final line of every report header section, the second column header line (a column separator line) is written to the report, visually delineating the column titles from the transaction detail data lines.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Write Column Header Line 2
Column Separator Line

acceptance_criteria.Given: Column Header Line 1 has been successfully written to the report file and the Line Counter has been incremented
acceptance_criteria.When: The system continues executing the Write Headers procedure (1120-WRITE-HEADERS) after writing Column Header Line 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: Column Header Line 2 (TRANSACTION-HEADER-2), serving as a column separator line, is written as the fourth and final line of the header section to the report output file, and the Line Counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1, completing the header section

rules.rule_name: Increment Line Counter for Each Header Line Written
rules.rule_description: The Line Counter is incremented by 1 each time any header line is written to the report. Since the header section consists of 4 lines (Report Name, Blank Line, Column Header 1, Column Header 2), the Line Counter is incremented 4 times in total per header section, ensuring accurate page size tracking.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Increment Line Counter
for Each Header Line Written

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Write Headers procedure (1120-WRITE-HEADERS) is executing and any one of the four header lines (Report Name Header, Blank Line, Column Header Line 1, or Column Header Line 2) has just been written to the report output file
acceptance_criteria.When: Each individual header line is successfully written to the report file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Line Counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1 immediately after each header line is written, resulting in a total increment of 4 to the Line Counter upon completion of the full header section, which is used to determine when the next page size limit is reached

rules.rule_name: Detect First Transaction to Trigger Report Initialization
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the current transaction being processed is the very first transaction in the report run, using the first-time processing flag to decide whether report initialization steps should be executed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this the First Transaction? WS-FIRST-TIME = Y

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction report writing process has been invoked for a transaction record, and the first-time processing flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is set to 'Y' indicating no transaction has been processed yet in this report run
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the first-time processing flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) to determine if this is the first transaction being written to the report
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies this as the first transaction and proceeds to initialize the report by populating the report date range headers and writing the report headers to the output report file

rules.rule_name: Mark First-Time Processing Flag as Completed
rules.rule_description: Once the first transaction is detected and report initialization begins, the first-time processing flag is immediately updated to prevent repeated report header initialization on subsequent transactions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark First-Time Flag as Processed
Set WS-FIRST-TIME = N

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has confirmed that the first-time processing flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is 'Y', indicating this is the first transaction being processed in the current report run
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins the report initialization sequence for the first transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first-time processing flag (WS-FIRST-TIME) is set to 'N' so that subsequent transactions do not trigger report header initialization again during the same report run

rules.rule_name: Populate Report Header with Reporting Start Date
rules.rule_description: The reporting start date, which was read from the Date Parameters file at program startup, is stamped onto the report header so that the output report clearly identifies the beginning of the reporting period covered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Populate Report Header
with Reporting Start Date

acceptance_criteria.Given: This is the first transaction being processed, the first-time flag has been marked as processed, and the reporting start date (WS-START-DATE) has been previously loaded from the Date Parameters file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initializes the report header for the first time
acceptance_criteria.Then: The reporting start date (WS-START-DATE) is moved into the report header start date field (REPT-START-DATE) so that the report header displays the correct start of the reporting period

rules.rule_name: Populate Report Header with Reporting End Date
rules.rule_description: The reporting end date, which was read from the Date Parameters file at program startup, is stamped onto the report header so that the output report clearly identifies the end of the reporting period covered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Populate Report Header
with Reporting End Date

acceptance_criteria.Given: This is the first transaction being processed, the first-time flag has been marked as processed, and the reporting end date (WS-END-DATE) has been previously loaded from the Date Parameters file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initializes the report header for the first time
acceptance_criteria.Then: The reporting end date (WS-END-DATE) is moved into the report header end date field (REPT-END-DATE) so that the report header displays the correct end of the reporting period

rules.rule_name: Write Report Headers to Output Report on First Transaction
rules.rule_description: When the first transaction is being processed, the complete set of report headers is written to the output report file. The headers include the report name (with the populated start and end dates), a blank separator line, and two column heading lines that label the transaction detail columns.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Write Report Headers
to Output Report

acceptance_criteria.Given: This is the first transaction being processed, the first-time flag has been set to 'N', and both the reporting start date and end date have been populated into the report header fields (REPT-START-DATE and REPT-END-DATE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system writes the initial report headers to the output report file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The following four lines are written sequentially to the output report file and the line counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1 after each line is written: (1) the Report Name Header line containing the report title along with the reporting start and end dates, (2) a blank separator line, (3) Transaction Column Header Line 1 containing the first row of column labels, and (4) Transaction Column Header Line 2 containing the second row of column labels — resulting in the line counter being incremented by a total of 4

rules.rule_name: Evaluate Page Size Limit to Trigger Page Break
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the current report page has reached its maximum capacity of 20 lines, and if so, triggers the page break process including writing page totals and reprinting headers for the new page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Has Line Counter Reached Page Size Limit of 20?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction report is being generated and the line counter is being tracked for the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: The line counter value, when divided by the defined page size limit of 20, produces a remainder of zero (i.e., the line counter is an exact multiple of 20)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system determines the page is full and triggers the page total writing process followed by the header rewriting process for the new page; if the line counter is not a multiple of 20, the system proceeds directly to transaction amount accumulation and detail line writing without any page break

rules.rule_name: Write Accumulated Page Total to Report
rules.rule_description: When a page break is triggered, the accumulated page total amount is formatted and written as a page total summary line to the transaction report before the new page begins.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Accumulated Page Total to Report

acceptance_criteria.Given: The page size limit of 20 lines has been reached and a page break has been triggered
acceptance_criteria.When: The page total writing process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The accumulated page total amount stored in the working storage page total field is moved to the report page total display field, and the formatted page total line is written to the report output file

rules.rule_name: Accumulate Page Total into Grand Total
rules.rule_description: Each time a page is completed, the page's accumulated transaction total is added to the running grand total, ensuring the grand total reflects the sum of all completed page totals across the entire report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Add Page Total to Grand Total

acceptance_criteria.Given: A page break has been triggered and the current page total has been written to the report
acceptance_criteria.When: The page total is being finalized before resetting
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page total amount is added to the grand total accumulator, so that the grand total grows with each completed page's transaction sum

rules.rule_name: Reset Page Total to Zero After Page Break
rules.rule_description: After the page total has been written to the report and added to the grand total, the page total accumulator is reset to zero so that transaction amounts on the new page are accumulated fresh without carrying over amounts from the previous page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Page Total to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current page total has been written to the report and added to the grand total
acceptance_criteria.When: The page break finalization process is completing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page total accumulator is set to zero, ensuring that transaction amounts for the next page start accumulating from zero

rules.rule_name: Write Page Separator Line After Page Totals
rules.rule_description: After the page total line is written and the page total is reset, a separator line (Column Header Line 2) is written to the report to visually separate the page total section from the upcoming new page content, and the line counter is incremented accordingly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Page Separator Line to Report

acceptance_criteria.Given: The page total has been written to the report and the page total accumulator has been reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The page break process is concluding before new headers are written
acceptance_criteria.Then: The column header line 2 is written to the report as a visual separator line, and the line counter is incremented by one to account for this separator line

rules.rule_name: Write Report Name Header at Top of New Page
rules.rule_description: At the start of each new page following a page break, the report name header is written as the first line of the new page to identify the report, and the line counter is incremented to track the new page's line usage.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Report Name Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: A page break has been completed and a new page is being initialized
acceptance_criteria.When: The header writing process begins for the new page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The report name header line is written to the report output file as the first line of the new page, and the line counter is incremented by one

rules.rule_name: Write Blank Separator Line After Report Name Header
rules.rule_description: Immediately after the report name header is written on a new page, a blank line is inserted to visually separate the report name from the column headers, improving report readability.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Blank Separator Line

acceptance_criteria.Given: The report name header has been written as the first line of the new page
acceptance_criteria.When: The header writing process continues
acceptance_criteria.Then: A blank line is written to the report output file immediately after the report name header, and the line counter is incremented by one to account for the blank line

rules.rule_name: Write Column Header Line 1 with Date Range on New Page
rules.rule_description: After the blank separator line, the first column header line — which includes the reporting date range (start date and end date) — is written to the new page to provide context for the transactions listed below it.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Column Header Line 1 with Date Range

acceptance_criteria.Given: The report name header and blank separator line have been written on the new page
acceptance_criteria.When: The header writing process continues to the column headers
acceptance_criteria.Then: Transaction Header Line 1, which contains the reporting date range with the start date and end date, is written to the report output file, and the line counter is incremented by one

rules.rule_name: Write Column Header Line 2 to Complete New Page Header
rules.rule_description: The second column header line is written as the final element of the new page header block, completing the header section and establishing the column labels under which transaction detail lines will be listed on the new page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Column Header Line 2

acceptance_criteria.Given: The report name header, blank separator line, and column header line 1 have been written on the new page
acceptance_criteria.When: The header writing process reaches its final step
acceptance_criteria.Then: Transaction Header Line 2 is written to the report output file as the last line of the header block, and the line counter is incremented by one, after which the system proceeds to transaction amount accumulation and detail line writing

rules.rule_name: Page Break Trigger Based on Line Counter Reaching Page Size
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the current report page has reached its maximum line capacity of 20 lines, triggering page totals writing and new page header generation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Has Line Counter Reached Page Size of 20 Lines?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction detail line has just been written to the report and the line counter has been incremented
acceptance_criteria.When: The line counter value is checked and it is an exact multiple of the defined page size of 20 lines (i.e., line counter MOD 20 equals zero)
acceptance_criteria.Then: A page break is triggered: the page totals writing process is initiated followed by the new page headers writing process; if the line counter is NOT a multiple of 20, normal transaction processing continues without a page break

rules.rule_name: Format and Write Accumulated Page Total to Report
rules.rule_description: Formats the accumulated page total amount and writes it as a page total summary line to the transaction report at the end of each page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Accumulated Page Total for Report

acceptance_criteria.Given: A page break has been triggered because the line counter has reached the page size of 20 lines, and the page total accumulator (WS-PAGE-TOTAL) holds the sum of all transaction amounts on the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: The page totals writing process is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The accumulated page total amount is moved into the report page total field (REPT-PAGE-TOTAL), the formatted page total line (REPORT-PAGE-TOTALS) is written to the report output file as a new record

rules.rule_name: Accumulate Page Total into Grand Total
rules.rule_description: After writing the page total line, the page total amount is added to the running grand total, ensuring the grand total reflects the cumulative sum of all transaction amounts across all pages.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Add Page Total to Grand Total

acceptance_criteria.Given: The page total line has been written to the report and the current page total (WS-PAGE-TOTAL) contains the sum of all transaction amounts for the completed page
acceptance_criteria.When: The grand total accumulation step is executed immediately after writing the page total line
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page total amount (WS-PAGE-TOTAL) is added to the grand total accumulator (WS-GRAND-TOTAL), increasing the grand total by the exact amount of the completed page's transactions

rules.rule_name: Reset Page Total to Zero After Writing
rules.rule_description: After the page total has been written to the report and added to the grand total, the page total accumulator is reset to zero so that the next page begins accumulating transaction amounts fresh.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Page Total to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: The page total has been written to the report and added to the grand total accumulator
acceptance_criteria.When: The page total reset step is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page total accumulator (WS-PAGE-TOTAL) is set to zero, ensuring that transaction amounts on the next page are accumulated independently without carrying over amounts from the previous page

rules.rule_name: Write Page Separator Line After Page Total
rules.rule_description: After writing the page total and resetting it, a column header separator line (TRANSACTION-HEADER-2) is written to visually separate the page total from the new page content, and the line counter is incremented.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Page Separator Line

acceptance_criteria.Given: The page total has been written to the report and the page total accumulator has been reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The page separator writing step is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The column header separator line (TRANSACTION-HEADER-2) is written to the report output file as a new record, and the line counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1 to account for this separator line

rules.rule_name: Write Report Name Header on New Page
rules.rule_description: At the start of each new page following a page break, the report name header is written as the first line of the new page, and the line counter is incremented.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Report Name Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: A page break has occurred, page totals have been written, and the new page header writing process has been initiated
acceptance_criteria.When: The report name header writing step is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The report name header (REPORT-NAME-HEADER) is written to the report output file as the first record of the new page, and the line counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1

rules.rule_name: Write Blank Separator Line After Report Name Header
rules.rule_description: After the report name header is written on a new page, a blank line is inserted to visually separate the report name from the column headers, and the line counter is incremented.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Blank Separator Line

acceptance_criteria.Given: The report name header has been written as the first line of the new page
acceptance_criteria.When: The blank separator line writing step is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: A blank line (WS-BLANK-LINE) is written to the report output file immediately after the report name header, and the line counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1 to account for this blank line

rules.rule_name: Write Column Header Line 1 with Reporting Date Range
rules.rule_description: After the blank separator line, the first column header line is written to the new page. This header includes the reporting start date and end date that define the reporting period for the transaction report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Column Header Line 1 with Start and End Dates

acceptance_criteria.Given: The blank separator line has been written on the new page, and the reporting start date (WS-START-DATE) and end date (WS-END-DATE) have been set in the report header fields (REPT-START-DATE and REPT-END-DATE) during the initial report setup
acceptance_criteria.When: The first column header line writing step is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first transaction column header line (TRANSACTION-HEADER-1), which contains the reporting start date and end date, is written to the report output file, and the line counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1

rules.rule_name: Write Column Header Line 2 to Complete Page Header
rules.rule_description: After the first column header line, the second column header line is written to complete the page header section, providing the full column label structure for transaction detail lines on the new page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Column Header Line 2

acceptance_criteria.Given: The first column header line has been written on the new page
acceptance_criteria.When: The second column header line writing step is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The second transaction column header line (TRANSACTION-HEADER-2) is written to the report output file immediately after the first column header line, and the line counter (WS-LINE-COUNTER) is incremented by 1, completing the page header; normal transaction detail processing then continues on the new page
